messages:
jamie (AE): Hey team — Zenith Health POC on Android is hitting streaming failures. They see SSE disconnects ~10–15s in and the app throws a JSON parse error (partial chunk). CC @maria (SE) and @ravi (Android).

maria (SE): Thanks Jamie. Can you paste the minimal log + client stack trace? Also is this happening behind a corporate proxy / CDN / mobile network?

ravi (Android): Putting logs below. Happens on Pixel 6 and Samsung S22, Android SDK v0.9.1. Happens both on wifi and cell. Stack: 
```
2027-06-05 14:12:07.234 INFO okhttp3.EventSource: open
2027-06-05 14:12:19.512 WARN okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2Stream: Unexpected end of stream
2027-06-05 14:12:19.513 ERROR AppParser: java.io.EOFException: End of input at line 1 column 327
    at com.fasterxml.jackson.core.json.ReaderBasedJsonParser._constructError
```
Client shows IOException: "unexpected end of stream" and then Jackson EOF on parsing partial JSON chunk.

maria (SE): Ok that's helpful. Two quick suspects: (1) intermediate buffering/proxy (NGINX, ALB, corporate proxies) that coalesces or truncates chunk boundaries, (2) client read timeout / connection failure behavior on network changes.

maria (SE): Can you confirm response headers from our endpoint (curl -i)? Also try toggling a couple things on the client: increase read timeout, set retryOnConnectionFailure(true), and ensure Accept: text/event-stream.

ravi (Android): curl shows: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Server: redwood-inference
Cache-Control: no-cache
```
No X-Accel-Buffering header.

tess (eng): If there is no X-Accel-Buffering: no then some proxies (nginx default) will buffer and then send large coalesced chunks which can confuse some SSE parsers on mobile. We also had a bug where the Android SDK's chunk parser dropped zero-length chunks at TCP boundary. We shipped a fix in 0.9.2 — can you try using the latest SDK?

ravi (Android): We can test with 0.9.2 tomorrow. For immediate triage: is there a recommended server-side heartbeat? They said sometimes it dies when switching networks.

maria (SE): Yes — server heartbeat helps. Send a comment line every 10s, like `: keepalive\n\n`. That keeps connections alive across NATs and some mobile carriers. Also set small SSE buffer flushes on the server so nothing is coalesced for >5s.

ops-bot: server-log 1798123468: connection_close reason=client_closed_stream duration=12.12s peer_ip=52.14.23.41 route=/v1/generate?sse=true status=200 bytes_sent=3487

maria (SE): ops logs confirm client closed after ~12s. That points at client-side or middlebox dropping. Two actionable workarounds to try now:
- Client: bump OkHttp read timeout to 60s and enable retryOnConnectionFailure. Example: `new OkHttpClient.Builder().readTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS).retryOnConnectionFailure(true).build()`
- Server: enable `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (nginx) or disable response buffering in ALB. Add a lightweight comment heartbeat every 8–10s.

ravi (Android): Ran quick test with increased read timeout + heartbeat from server (we asked Redwood to enable heartbeat for this POC). Still saw one disconnect when phone switched from wifi->4g, but much less frequent. When it fails the app receives EOF and parser throws.

tess (eng): For network switches we recommend implementing a client reconnect + resume model. On reconnect, use tokenized resume or request the last seen token id. For now, fallback on streaming fallback to chunked polling for mobile builds if resume isn't possible.

security: Quick note from security — Zenith's IT says they can't whitelist IPs (dynamic mobile) and they prefer private deployment. This is an enterprise blocker for them if we can't guarantee connectivity.

jamie (AE): Understood. Pricing note for the record: for production POC at their scale we recommended Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) — helps with consistent ingress routing and can remove some public CDN buffering issues if connected via Private Link. I can share ballpark numbers offline with procurement.

maria (SE): Action items: (1) Ravi to test SDK v0.9.2 tomorrow and confirm if chunk parser fix helps; (2) Ops to keep heartbeat enabled for POC (we've already toggled); (3) Client implement simple reconnect + resume or fallback to polling; (4) Jamie to surface Dedicated + Private options to Zenith. If we need deeper debugging, ask for a short screen-share and a pcap from the device.

ravi (Android): Will test v0.9.2 and send results. Can we get a short window where Redwood toggles `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the POC route and keeps heartbeat for 24h?

maria (SE): Yes, we've requested it. Ops confirmed temporary change for the POC window.

jamie (AE): I'll follow up with Zenith on Private/VPC options and procurement asks.

maria (SE): Thanks everyone. If it still fails after SDK upgrade we'll collect a zip of logs + pcap and do a joint debug session. :+1"
